subject: HealthX SSQ: PII classification, access boundary & cross-border map
messages:
From: Elena Moroz <elena@healthx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, procurement@healthx.com
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthX security questionnaire — PII scope & transfers

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're starting the security & privacy review for Redwood as part of our vendor intake for the clinical routing project. Attached is our SSQ but the immediate items we need to unblock procurement are: a concise data flow map that highlights where PII (PHI-adjacent) is processed/temporarily stored, list of subprocessors with locations, KMS key custody details, and the proposed DPA Annex A language for cross-border transfers.

Key asks (short):
- Do you process EU-sourced patient identifiers? If so, can you commit to EU residency options or explain fallback routing?
- Subprocessor roster and whether any subprocessors have access to raw PII (tokenized vs cleartext).
- Retention windows for inference logs and request/response artifacts.
- Provide SOC 2 snapshot and KMS attestation (HSM/KMS provider + key rotation cadence).

Procurement is on a tight cadence — can you circle back with the items above and a 72-hour timeline?

Regards,
Elena Moroz
Senior Information Security Manager | HealthX
[attachment: HealthX_SSQ_2028.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moroz <elena@healthx.com>
Cc: procurement@healthx.com
Date: 2028-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthX security questionnaire — PII scope & transfers

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick plan and deliverables:

Deliverables (within 72 hours):
- Annotated data flow diagram (attached: Redwood_Dataflow_v1.pdf) showing where raw identifiers may appear and where tokens/KV caches are used.
- Subprocessor roster with access level flags (will provide CSV).
- Initial redline of DPA Annex A for transfers (DPA_Annex_A_redline.docx).
- SOC2 snapshot + KMS attestation (SOC2_snapshot_2027.pdf + KMS statement).

Short answers:
- EU data: Redwood supports region-based routing for hosted customers; for HealthX we can commit to EU residency for EU-sourced records via a dedicated tenant and routing policy (requires a simple config add and an Annex).
- Subprocessors: most ML infra subprocessors operate on tokenized payloads; a small set (GPU providers for Dedicated offering) may handle decrypted inputs when configured — we'll flag those in the roster.
- Retention: default inference logs are 30 days; we have configurable retention down to 0 days for sensitive workloads.

I'm attaching the first-pass data flow and will follow up with the full roster + redlined Annex. Looping in Legal and Security for any compliance notes.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_Dataflow_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Elena Moroz <elena@healthx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthx.com
Date: 2028-06-02T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthX security questionnaire — PII scope & transfers

Thanks Tessa — that looks promising. A few clarifications before procurement will accept the Annex:

1) EU residency commitment: we require at-rest residency for EU-subject records. An operational routing note saying "EU-sourced requests will be served from EU tenant only" plus an SLA measuring misrouted requests is necessary.
2) Subprocessor access: we need a statement of whether any subprocessors can access cleartext PII and, if yes, the control set (MFA, limited admin keys, record-level audit).
3) Retention: procurement requests a 90/30/0 template (90 days by default, 30 days for sensitive flagged requests, 0 for opt-out customers) — can you confirm Redwood supports that configuration?
4) Please include a copy of your latest SOC 2 Type II or a reasonable snapshot; procurement will accept a redaction if needed.

If you can provide the redlined Annex + corrected dataflow (showing residency guardrails) and the KMS attestation by end of day tomorrow, we'll keep the review on schedule.

On a side note: are there any subprocessors located in RU/CN we should be aware of for export controls?

Best,
Elena

Tessa / Neha — quick legal read:
- Annex redline looks good overall. I suggest two edits: 1) tighten the definition of "EU-sourced requests" to avoid downstream ambiguity (proposed wording attached as inline comments in the docx), and 2) limit remedies to measurable SLAs (avoid open-ended indemnity language tied to routing misconfiguration).
- We can commit to a tenant-routing residency approach (we cannot guarantee physical at-rest encryption key location for certain Dedicated setups unless we have an explicit infrastructure boundary in the contract). We'll add a clear statement about the mechanism (routing + tenant isolation + audit logs).

Neha — can you add the KMS attestation text and confirm whether any subprocessors have cleartext access? If yes, enumerate controls (MFA, role separation, audit) and provide SOC artifact reference.

I'll incorporate small legal edits and send a consolidated packet to Elena.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
